stories.title: Physical Superintelligence (PSI) says its internal research system, running a non-public Anthropic model, proved the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture (open since 2008): bounded low-degree polynomials have an influential variable, so quantum computers get at most a polynomial speed-up on random inputs; proof found on day 3 of a run, checked in Lean, improved twice; Stanford's Blanc, Docter, Strassle and Tan call it 'a huge result'
Bloomberg: OpenAI has closed about $11B of a new round at a $1.25T valuation, which could reach ~$20B in total; well short of the $30B it was reported to be seeking in September

Wired: Vals finds open-weight models nearly match gated cyber models on multi-step attacks against mock corporate networks: OpenAI's trusted-access Daybreak completed 81% of tasks, DeepSeek 73%, equal on some tasks; an attack cost $17-46 in tokens with GPT-6 Sol vs $2-3 with DeepSeek

House China, Foreign Affairs and Intelligence chairs ask Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing on 18 Nov after the NYT reported US intelligence concluded Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was recruited by China's MSS to gather intelligence on him; Nvidia rejects the claims; Democrats set to step up oversight of Nvidia

UK government adds a clause to the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill (Lords third reading) letting ministers regulate how essential-service and digital providers deploy AI agents: safeguards against loss of control, incident notification, evidence preservation and government-led reviews, possibly with inspectors who can enter premises and seize documents

Ramp data: business token spend grew only 1.5% across August and September after +42% month on month in July, even as token volumes rose; the top 1% of firms dipped just below ~$10,000 per employee per month; median firms spend $12-15, the top 10% $600-1,000

Bank of England's November Monetary Policy Report: firms estimate AI has raised UK productivity by about 0.5% over three years (0.1-0.2 points a year since early 2024); AI accounts for just under a fifth of UK GDP growth since early 2026, mostly from building and deploying AI rather than using it; virtually no net effect on hiring yet

AE Studio test (AI Alignment Foundation hackathon): nine coding agents given a private token and access to a forum of 24 other agents posted the token in 15% of 181 trials and ran an untrusted install script 24% of the time when the swarm demanded it in exchange for a bug fix, vs 2% and 0% on an ordinary help forum

CERT-In releases AI Security Auditing Guidelines (4 Nov): a risk-tiered framework for auditing AI systems developed, bought, deployed or run in India, or serving Indian users, across nine domains (governance, data, model risk, bias, explainability, security and incident reporting, monitoring, human oversight, AI supply chain), with extra requirements for generative, RAG, agentic and autonomous systems

Hightouch tests decision models (TypeSafe's Jev, OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna) against frontier LLMs on grading identity resolution: decision models are up to 90x cheaper and 10x faster ($0.05-0.10 per 1,000 identities, ~0.15s) but trail Opus by ~6 points on hard cases; because Jev's errors come with low confidence, routing those to Claude Opus gets near-Opus accuracy at over 4x lower cost (HN ~300 points)

Underdog (Conway Research) releases Woof, a ~40MB English text-to-speech model with two voices that runs on a laptop CPU with only numpy (13.8x real time on one thread) and in the browser; its card claims 1.42% word error rate on Gradium's TTS Hard Cases, 25% fewer errors than a 41.5GB model; weights on Hugging Face under a non-commercial licence

Palo Alto Networks is in talks to buy Clutch Security, which controls AI agents' access to company systems (non-human identity), for $500M in cash plus milestone payouts, about 50x its ~$10M ARR; it would be Palo Alto's seventh acquisition this year (TechCrunch, after The Information)

Meta launches Spaces for its Muse agents: describe an idea and Muse builds a tracker, planner or project board in the sidebar that stays updated from connected apps in the background; Zuckerberg says he built a BBQ game, event tracker and home-control dashboard; Muse had 10M US and Canadian users by October

Meta indefinitely pauses its commercial-terms update that would have required Business account holders, including news publishers, to let Meta crawl linked external sites (and bypass paywalls with test credentials) for AI development; courts in Brazil and Norway had issued injunctions and the UK CMA opened an investigation

Wired: data brokers pitch companies $350K-$2M one-off fees for old work records (documents, emails, Slack messages, tickets, call transcripts) to sell to labs including Anthropic and OpenAI for training; Handshake confirms it licenses professional documents and buys students' coursework; start-ups now broker the data of companies winding down

Quess Corp's India GCC Tech Talent report (Q2 FY27, Jul-Sep 2026): AI, data and cybersecurity rose to 30.3% of global capability centre tech hiring demand from 25.8%; supply gaps of 38-42% in AI, data and analytics and 30-35% in cybersecurity; 87-88% of advanced-skill hiring stays in tier-1 cities, but Coimbatore grew ~30% quarter on quarter and tier-2 cities 13%

Indian payments firm Cashfree launches Checkout for Agents, built on the open WebMCP standard: merchants' checkout pages tell AI agents the order total and payment options directly, which Cashfree says cuts agents' token use by over 40%, with no merchant code changes; the user still authorises the payment

Crusoe says Google has acquired its southeast Wyoming data-centre site after Crusoe completed site selection, approvals and a hybrid power plan with Tallgrass Energy (fuel cells, grid, gas turbines, planned carbon capture); Bloomberg reports Crusoe failed to sign customers, including Google, for the project

Physicl, from nfinite founder Alex de Vigan, raises a $10M seed led by Inovia Capital to turn messy real-world data into physically accurate 3D simulations for training robots and world models on hard edge cases; launches Studio with 10,000 3D environments and 100,000 assets

PyTorch 2.15 ships a rewritten NCCL backend for GPU-to-GPU communication, aimed at diagnosing and recovering from a single failing GPU without restarting a whole training job; the old ProcessGroupNCCL could spawn dozens of communicators per process group and cause intermittent deadlocks

Unconfirmed (The Information, seen only as a Techmeme summary): TSMC is considering moving into 3D DRAM manufacturing at the request of Nvidia, its largest customer, amid the AI-driven memory shortage

Anthropic IPO: the FT reports it still plans to list before Thanksgiving, raising $80-100B at a $1.25-1.75T valuation; Bloomberg says potential buyers see it as low as $1.1T (vs ~$2T a month ago); Reuters says backers doubt the roadshow can start next week; October revenue is missing from the updated S-1
